review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: Split the combined source-inconsistency limitation into separate entries and verified each against the literal text: CDVA p=0.06 (abstract) vs p=0.15 (results, discussion) and OR 29.41 (abstract, discussion) vs OR 0.034 (results) and 40°F (surgical technique) vs 100-120 fahrenheit (discussion) kept as source conflicts.
Reclassified 12.6% (results) vs 12% in a sample of 95 eyes (discussion) as a rounding ambiguity rather than a source conflict, per the rulings.
Noted that OR 0.034 is approximately the reciprocal of 29.41 without asserting the source meaning.
Added a limitation that the discussion restates the p=0.15 comparison as BCVA while the results call it CDVA.
unresolved: Disposition aggregate_only: the source is a retrospective single-centre case series of 20 eyes of 17 patients reported only as counts, means, ranges, percentages and p-values; no patient has individual identity evidence or an individually described course, so no individual patient records are created and cohort statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 17 (literal, "20 eyes of 17 patients") and roster_complete is false because none of the 17 stated individuals can be enumerated.

The Methods give the study period as January 2012 to May 2017 for identification from records, while the introduction gives January 2014 to December 2017 and the results describe a 5-year study period; these are not reconciled.

Source conflict: the p-value for the difference in mean CDVA before surgery versus the last follow-up is printed as p=0.06 in the abstract and p=0.15 in the results and discussion; not reconciled and not used as a label.

Source conflict: the odds ratio for epithelial ingrowth after enhancement versus primary LASIK is printed as 29.41 in the abstract and discussion ("29 times greater" in the discussion) and as OR 0.034 in the results; 0.034 is approximately the reciprocal of 29.41, so the results value may express the inverse comparison, but the source does not say so; not reconciled and not used as a label.
Ambiguity (rounding, not a conflict): the incidence after enhancement is printed as 12.6% in the results and as a 12% incidence in a sample of 95 eyes in the discussion.
Source conflict: the temperature of the compressed heating air flow is printed as 40°F in the surgical technique and as between 100-120 fahrenheit (F) in the discussion; not reconciled.
The discussion calls the visual acuity measure BCVA when restating the p=0.15 comparison that the results report for CDVA; terminology recorded as printed.
The duration between LASIK and epithelial ingrowth treatment is called a median but is printed with a mean-style standard deviation (85.1 ± 98 days); recorded as printed, not interpreted.
The abstract and results text describe both patients (17) and eyes (20); statements are not attributed to individual eyes or patients.
Figure 1 is one slit lamp photograph of an unidentified patient of the series; pixels are described only in visual.json and ownership stays unresolved.
No supplements are listed by the source.

key_findings: Read all 30 segments (no tables, no supplements): retrospective series of 20 eyes of 17 patients reported only as counts, means, ranges, percentages and p-values; no individuated patient narrative, per-patient table or case description anywhere, so aggregate_only with patients [] is correct.

The only singular patient reference is the Figure 1 caption ('a patient with chronic foreign-body sensation'), which does not identify which of the 17 patients or 20 eyes is shown; figure ownership stays unresolved.
Roster: reported_individual_count 17 from '20 eyes of 17 patients', roster_complete false.
Study period variants (January 2014 to December 2017; January 2012 to May 2017; 5-year study period) and 'Median duration ... 85.1 ± 98 days' verified literal.
residual_risks: A downstream consumer could argue the Figure 1 caption alone describes one individual; it was not made a patient record because it has no identity link to the series.
